# subtrack

Keep track of your subscriptions from the terminal: what they cost you each month, and what renews next.
Plain Node.js (ES modules), no dependencies.

```sh
subtrack add Netflix 12.99                        # monthly by default, first charge today
subtrack add "Domain name" 14 --every year --since 2026-03-02
subtrack list                                     # every plan with its monthly cost
subtrack total                                    # what all of it costs you a month
subtrack renewals --within 14                     # charges coming up in the next 14 days, soonest first
subtrack export > subs.csv                        # CSV for a spreadsheet
subtrack remove Netflix
```

During development, run it with `node bin/subtrack.js <command>`.

## Options

| Option | Commands | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--every month\|year` | add | How often the plan charges you (default `month`). |
| `--since YYYY-MM-DD` | add | Date of the first charge (default today). Later charges fall on the same day of the month, or the last day of a shorter month. |
| `--within <days>` | renewals | How far ahead to look (default 30). A charge today counts. |
| `--today YYYY-MM-DD` | list, renewals, export | Pretend today is another date. |
| `--file <path>` | all | Where your subscriptions are kept. Default: `$SUBTRACK_FILE`, else `./subscriptions.json`. |

## Money

Prices are typed in euros (`12.99`, `1,299.00`) and kept in whole cents. The monthly cost of a yearly plan is its
price divided by 12.

## Code

- `bin/subtrack.js`: the command line
- `src/cycles.js`: billing cycles: monthly cost and next charge of a plan
- `src/renewals.js`: upcoming charges
- `src/export.js`: CSV export
- `src/store.js`: reading and writing the subscriptions file
- `src/dates.js`, `src/money.js`: date and money helpers

Run the tests with `npm test`.

content.text:
Weekly plans work, and monthly costs now round to the nearest cent. All 38 tests pass (32 of 33 before). Changes are uncommitted in the working tree.

**What you asked for**
- `subtrack add "Meal kit" 59.90 --every week` works, alongside `month` and `year`. `weekly` and `week` both work, like the existing `monthly` and `yearly` aliases.
- A weekly plan's monthly cost is price × 52 ÷ 12, rounded to the cent. €12 a week shows €52.00 a month, and €59.90 a week shows €259.57. It shows the same way in `list`, `total`, `add` output and `export`.
- Weekly charges fall every 7 days from `--since`, and `renewals` lists them like any other plan.
- Monthly costs round to the nearest cent instead of cutting. €119.99 a year shows €10.00 a month.

**Things I changed beyond the literal request**
- **Renewals sort bug (pre-existing).** `renewals` sorted by the display label ("2 Nov" before "30 Oct"), so charges across a month boundary came out in the wrong order. One test already failed on this before I touched anything. Weekly plans would hit it constantly, so I sort by the ISO date now.
- **File loading.** The old 0.1 upgrade step turned any cycle that wasn't "year" into monthly, so a stored `weekly` plan would have silently become monthly on the next run. It now only renames the legacy `month`/`year` values.
- **CSV export** had its own copy of the monthly maths, so it now uses the shared function. This means yearly plans in CSV exports also round now (119.99 → 10.00 rather than 9.99).
- **Docs.** README options and money section updated.

**Not done**
- I didn't bump the version in `package.json` (still 0.3.0) or commit anything. Say if you want either.
